pages.title: Data transfer Instructions
pages.text:
Data transfer Instructions:

Move destination, source
Source can be register, memory location, immediate operand.
both can't be memory location at the same time

MOV AX, CS:[21h]
MOV AL, CH
MOV [220h], BX
MOV X, AX
MOV X, Y ✗

stack operations:
Push AX - Pop AX - PushA AX - PopA AX
it's can be any register - memory location

address transfer:
LEA register, source
LEA BX, [DI] <-> mov BX, offset [DI]
to get the address of DI "first char" and store it in BX

Arithmetic Instructions:

-ADD destination, source
with add operation we can add byte to byte or word to word like:
ADD AL, CL [AL=AL+CL] / But ADD AL, BL is ✗
ADD CH, DL [CH=CH+DL]
byte to word is wrong
8 bits  16 bits

If Carry flag CF=1 then we have
ADC AX, 15H = AX= AX + 15H + 1
- INC source : increase register or source by 1
if AX=8  INC AX -> AX=9
- AAA -> it correct the content of AL

For Subtraction:

- SUB Destination, source  Same as Add
SUB AX, 4H => AX=AX-4H
- DEC source: decrease source by 1
- NEG source change the sign of the source (opposite sign)

pages.title: I2207 - Page 2
pages.text:
I2207  ②  16-5-2025

- SBB destination, source : Subtract with Borrow/carry
Like if the Carry Flag CF = 1 it decrement the answer by 1
Ex: Mov AX, 12H  first we make AX=12H
SCF  this change the nb of CF from 0 to 1
SBB AX, 5  Subtract AX = AX - 5 - 1 [carry flag] = 6H

- CMP destination, source : Compare two specific bytes or words and so on do an instruction according to the result.
CMP AX, 7H  this compare AL with 7 by subtracting them
JNZ end; from each other
if Not zero jump to end.

For multiplication:
- MUL source : it multiply byte by byte or word by word.
1. if source is 1 byte then AL is multiplied by it and stored in AX
Mov AL, 12
Mov BL, 2
Mul BL -> BL x AL
AX = 24 -> stored in AX

2. if source is word then AX is multiplied by it and stored in DX:AX
(DX is upper, AX is lower)
Mov AX, 0FFF1H
Mov BX, 3
MUL BX -> BX x AX
DX = 2, AX = FFD3

- IMUL source:
Same as Mul but it consider signs.

For Division:
- DIV source: it divides ...

pages.title: Variable Declaration and Input/Output
pages.text:
if source is 1 word, (DX:AX) is divided by source,
and AX = quotient  DX = remainder

- IDIV : is signed division instruction

Variable declaration in assembly:

DB : Define byte (8 bits) ; X db ? (uninitialized variable)
DW : Define word (16 bits) / X dw 5  Y dw ?
DD : Define double word (32 bits)
DP : 48 bits
DQ : Define quad word (64 bits)

Read/Input Variables:

To enter a character with the keyboard we do:
Mov AH, 1 -> the function 1 used to read char
int 21h -> interrupt 21h
The input is stored in AL. And the number is stored as a character to use it as a number:
Sub AL, 48 OR Sub AL, '0'

Mov AH, 7
int 21h

Write or Display:

mov DL, 'A' -> you enter the character you want
mov AH, 2 -> to display to DL and then do this:
int 21h -> we can read only one digit at a time

Display a message:

* mov DX, offset variable OR Lea DX, variable
mov AH, 9 -> to display a message
int 21h

pages.title: I2207 - Page 3
pages.text:
I2207  ③  17-5-2025

If, else condition :

We use cmp to solve if-else in assembly
cmp source, destination -> to get the result of cmp, then
Jxx address of Lable -> jump to address of Lable

jl : jump if less , jle : jump if less or equal , je : jump if equal
jne : jump if not equal , jg : jump if greater , jge : jump if greater or equal , jnz : jump if not equal zero , jz : jump if equal zero

If we need to use jump without any condition we use jmp address of Lable

Logical instructions:

- Not source : convert all the bits in a byte or word. Ex: 00110110 -> 11001001
- And destination, source : do and operation over all bits
- OR destination, source : or operation on bits
- XOR destination, source : xor operation on bits
If you have trouble understanding this check page 5, week 3

Shift instruction:

- SHL destination, count (shift left)
It moves the most left bit to AL = 10110110 -> SHL AL, 3
the left and add zero at AL = 10110000
the beggining and add the moved bit in CF
- SHR destination, count (shift right)
Same as SHL but in the other direction
Like AL = 00101111
SHR AL, 1 => 00010111 CF=1

pages.title: Shift, Rotate, and Loop Instructions
pages.text:
- SAR source, count (Shift Arithmetic Right)
would the new bit according to AL = 10111001
the sign of the number, if it is negative SAR AL, 3
it add 1s else it add 0s AL = 11110111
- SAL destination, count (shift arithmetic left)
Same as SAR

Rotate instruction:

- Rol destination, count (Rotate left)
it rotate the bits in a byte or word. Ex: 10110111
so the left bit become the right and ROL AL, 1
it is also added to the CF also 01101111 CF=1

- ROR destination, count (Rotate right)
Same as Rol

- RCL destination, count (Rotate through carry Left)
In this instruction the first left bit is stored in the CF and the previous CF is added as the first right bit

- RCR
Same as RCL

Loop

- for: cmp cl, 4
jg end loop
add S, cl
inc cl
jmp for
end loop:

this is the way to write for loop

- while: cmp si, 4
jg end while
add S, si
inc si
jmp while
end while:

and this is the way to use while loop

pages.title: I2209 - Page 1
pages.text:
I2209:  ①  19-5-2025

Proposition: can be written p, q, r... and it is a proposed statement
Logical connections:
- And (∧) : and two propositions and it is true when both are true
- Or (∨) : will be true if either p or q are true
- If then (->) : if p true then q should be true "called implies"
- If and only if (<->) : this is true when p and q are the same either true or false
- Negation - Not (¬) :

Tautologies & consistency:

- Tautology iff V(θ) = T with any formula (⊨)
- Consistent iff V(θ) = T ∃ one θ where it is true
- Inconsistent iff V(θ) = F ∀ θ (is called contradiction)
Logical consequence : θ ⊨ λ => if V(θ)=T then V(λ)=T
Logical equivalences : θ ≡ λ iff V(θ)=V(λ) and ⊨ θ
* Page 59 in pdf for memorize (the last one rule in both columns are True?)
Note : ⊨ (tautology)
⊢ (logical consequence)

Semantic Tableau system:

Rules table: ¬¬p, p∧q, p∨q, p->q, p<->q
¬(p∧q), ¬(p∨q), ¬(p->q), ¬(p<->q)

- It is better ...
- Set is inconsistent ...
- Set is consistent ...

pages.title: Rules of Inference and Resolution
pages.text:
branch is closed if there is X & ¬X in the same root.

Rules of inference :

Modus Ponens (law of detachment - mode that affirms):
if a conditional statement and its hypothesis are true then the conclusion must also be true
p -> q conditional statement
p hypothesis
∴ q conclusion
Important table page 70 (Rules of inference)

- Satisfiability (SAT) and Propositional resolution

p -> q
q -> r
∴ p -> r

Literal is : p or ¬p
clause is : p or ¬p or p∨q∨r {p}, {¬p}, {p, q, r}
Conversion to clausal
- p ∨ q -> {p, q}
- p ∧ q -> {p}, {q}
the empty clause is unsatisfiable

Proof by refutation or contradiction:

Γ ⊨ A iff Γ ∪ {¬A} is unsatisfiable
to prove that Γ logical consequence of A we should take the negation of the conclusion (¬A) and prove that it leads to an empty clause.

How to prove
{p -> q, q -> r} ⊨ p -> r?
1 - Convert this to clausal:
p -> q => {¬p, q} ①
q -> r => {¬q, r} ②
¬(p -> r) => {p}, {¬r} ③, ④
then number them
and last derive them from each other

pages.title: I2207 - Page 4
pages.text:
I2207  ④  23-5-2025

Processor control instructions:

STC : Set Carry Flag to 1
STD : Set direction Flag to 1
STI : Set Interrupt flag to 1
CLC : Clear Carry Flag to 0
CLD : Clear direction Flag to 0
CLI : Clear interrupt flag to 0
CMC : Complement CF

Note : JNC means if CF = 0, JNS means if SF = 0
SF : get the bit in the MSB, after an operation (add-sub) so we can determine the sign of a number
PF : if the number of 1 bits is even then it is set to 1 if the number is odd then it is cleared to 0
AF : contain the carry bit from the fourth bit to the fifth one

Loop Instructions:

First we should define CX (count) the nb of repetition and then start the loop ex: for:
Loop for
and the CX value will automatically decrease by 1 each loop without do/cnt that normaly
Do - while loop:
same as for but use do
Loop do

Array:

A db 10 dup(0), create an array that 10 element and fill them with 0
A db 10, 2, 7, 6, ... to create string?
A dw 2, 5, 12, ...
* Only si & di can be used to indicate an element in array A[SI], A[DI]
- to move to a new line when display use : new line db 10, 13, '$'
